findings.highlight: when Tohsaka and Fuji-nee come home
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂か藤ねえが帰ってくるまで
findings.governingReading: The session would last until Tohsaka or Fuji-nee came home.
findings.explanation: Training planned to continue until either Rin or Taiga returned becomes a wait for both of them.

findings.evidenceJa: 無遠慮な視線をセイバーに向ける
findings.governingReading: Issei directs an unrestrained, socially inconsiderate look at the unfamiliar Saber.
findings.explanation: The narration changes an unabashed, inconsiderate stare into an intent gaze. Issei's coldness toward strangers remains explicit immediately afterward.

findings.highlight: in broad terms, nothing I've said is entirely untrue
findings.evidenceJa: 大きな目で見れば嘘は付いていないと思うぞ
findings.governingReading: He accepts the cover story as not really a lie when viewed generously, though Saber supplied most of it.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s thought that, broadly speaking, he is not lying becomes a claim about things he himself has said.

findings.highlight: Japanese tea for Issei, black tea for Saber.
findings.evidenceJa: 一成は日本茶、セイバーは紅茶でいいんだよな
findings.governingReading: He checks that Issei wants Japanese tea and Saber is fine with black tea.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s question about each person’s tea becomes a firm assignment.

findings.highlight: have a casual conversations with your friend from school
findings.evidenceJa: ご学友と気軽な話などできないでしょう
findings.governingReading: Saber worries her presence will prevent casual conversation between school friends.
findings.explanation: “A casual conversations” mismatches singular article and plural noun.

findings.governingReading: His old-fashioned, biased joke contrasts women generally with the “modest” Saber.
findings.explanation: Issei’s claim that women are noisy becomes the softer claim that girls may be chatty.

findings.highlight: Saber is fairly opinionated for some reason.
findings.evidenceJa: なぜかきっぱりと言うセイバー
findings.governingReading: She distinctly and decisively asks for Japanese tea as well.
findings.explanation: Saber stating her tea preference firmly becomes her being “opinionated.”

findings.highlight: I asked a few sly questions to find out if anything unusual was going on
findings.evidenceJa: なにか異状は起きていないかと注意深く聞いてみた
findings.governingReading: During the school talk, he listens attentively for any indication that something abnormal occurred.
findings.explanation: Shirou carefully listening for signs of trouble becomes him asking several sly questions.

findings.highlight: Saber needs to be with me tomorrow too.
findings.evidenceJa: 明日もセイバーに付き合ってもらわないといけない
findings.governingReading: He says he must have Saber keep him company or work with him tomorrow as well.
findings.explanation: Shirou needing Saber to accompany him becomes Saber needing to be with him.

findings.highlight: I saw that her spirit and soul are pure.
findings.evidenceJa: あの子の霊気は澄んでいた
findings.governingReading: He says her 霊気, spiritual presence or aura, was clear.
findings.explanation: Issei’s perception of a clear spiritual aura becomes seeing both Saber’s spirit and soul as pure.

findings.highlight: when her spirit is on full display like that
findings.evidenceJa: あれぐらい飛び抜けていると
findings.governingReading: Issei normally cannot judge such things, but Saber’s presence stands out so far that even an amateur can perceive it.
findings.explanation: Saber’s aura being extraordinarily pronounced becomes her spirit being “on full display.”

findings.governingReading: Shirou says Saber may be a little unsociable.

findings.highlight: you really shouldn't worry yourself over something like that
findings.evidenceJa: そのあたりは己で悩め
findings.governingReading: After rejecting Shirou’s odd interpretation, Issei says he should puzzle over that part for himself, because everything begins with self-questioning.
findings.explanation: Issei tells Shirou to worry or think through the matter himself; the English tells him not to worry about it.
